articles.title: Israel launches ground operation in central Gaza, dozens flee
articles.description: By Nidal al-Mughrabi and Mahmoud IssaCAIRO, Nov 18 (Reuters) - Dozens of displaced Palestinians fled their tents and shelters in central Gaza on Wednesday after Israel launched a rare ground raid in an area it withdrew from under a 2025 ceasefire.The ground advance, with Israeli tanks rolling along the main north-south Salahudeen road, came as the US-backed body overseeing the truce accused both Israel and Hamas militants of failing to meet their commitments to end hostilities.

articles.title: Israeli Tanks Advance Across Gaza Cease-Fire Line in Rare Incursion
articles.description: The Israeli military said it was conducting a limited raid into territory controlled by Hamas to address a threat. The militant group accused Israel of violating the truce.

articles.title: Israeli military begins a new thrust in Gaza, witnesses say
articles.description: By Nidal al-MughrabiCAIRO, Nov 18 (Reuters) - Israeli tanks advanced in an area of the central Gaza Strip on Wednesday, witnesses said, and the Israeli military said its forces were targeting Hamas infrastructure outside areas that Israel controls in the enclave.Witnesses said some Israeli tanks rolled onto the main Salahudeen road, west of the Yellow Line that marks the boundary of the two-thirds of the Gaza Strip still under Israeli control despite a ceasefire that has lasted more than a year.

articles.title: Trump's Board of Peace faults Israel and Hamas for failure to end Gaza war
articles.description: JERUSALEM, Nov 18 - The body overseeing US President Donald Trump's plan to end the Gaza war accused both Israel and Hamas of failing to meet their commitments to end hostilities, leaving the population of Gaza in dire conditions and the ceasefire in danger of collapse. Read more at straitstimes.com.

articles.title: Trump's Board of Peace faults Israel and Hamas for failure to end Gaza war
articles.description: By Alexander CornwellJERUSALEM, Nov 18 (Reuters) - The body overseeing US President Donald Trump's plan to end the Gaza war accused both Israel and Hamas of failing to meet their commitments to end hostilities, leaving the population of Gaza in dire conditions and the ceasefire in danger of collapse.The 12-page Board of Peace report, seen by Reuters, is the body's second to the United Nations Security Council since the US-backed ceasefire came into effect 13 months ago. It offers a sobering assessment of progress made since then.

articles.title: Board of Peace delivers bleak report on Gaza, warning of ceasefire collapse without immediate action
articles.description: The Board of Peace overseeing the Gaza ceasefire between Israel and Hamas and charged with handling the reconstruction of the war-shattered Palestinian territory has delivered a bleak report on its progress to the United Nations Security Council. The report calls on all parties to live up to their commitments under the agreement. It warns that continued delays will doom the chances of restoring peace and stability to Gaza. In its conclusion, the report says, “The distance between what has been agreed and what is happening on the ground nonetheless remains the principal risk to the process.”
